title: Basic Autoclave Safety

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Core precautions for safely operating an autoclave, which uses high-pressure, high-temperature steam and carries burn, scald, and pressure-vessel hazards independent of any biological hazard.
explanation: Autoclaves are pressure vessels operating well above atmospheric pressure and above the boiling point of water at that pressure — improper loading, opening, or venting can cause serious burns or projectile hazards. These are physical/mechanical hazards present regardless of the biological agent being sterilized.
keyPractices: Never open the autoclave door before pressure has returned to zero/ambient, as indicated by the gauge.
Use appropriate heat-resistant gloves and a face shield when removing hot loads.
Do not overfill or seal containers of liquid tightly — sealed containers can rupture or explode under autoclave conditions; allow venting as instructed by the equipment manual.
Follow the manufacturer's loading guidance — improper loading affects both sterilization efficacy and safety.
Report any unusual noise, pressure behavior, or door-seal issue and take the unit out of service until inspected.
commonMistakes: Attempting to force the door open when a gauge still shows residual pressure.
Tightly sealing a liquid-filled container before autoclaving.
